'''Andrew Berry''' (born 1963) is a British evolutionary biologist and historian of science with a particular interest in [[Alfred Russel Wallace]].  Previously, he was a Junior Fellow at the [[Harvard Society of Fellows]] and he is currently a lecturer in [[Evolutionary Biology|Organismic and Evolutionary Biology]] at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="Harvard">{{cite web|title=Harvard Profiles|date=3 March 2025 |url=http://harvardscience.harvard.edu/directory/researchers/andrew-berry|publisher=Harvard University}}</ref>

==Early life==
Andrew Berry was born in 1963 in London. His father is biologist [[R. J. Berry]]. He was educated at [[Shrewsbury School]] and then studied [[Zoology]] at [[St John's College, Oxford]]. He did his PhD under [[Martin Kreitman]] in [[Extended evolutionary synthesis|evolutionary genetics]] at [[Princeton University]].<ref name="Web1"/> At Harvard, he did post-doctoral work in [[Richard Lewontin]]'s lab.

==Career==
Berry's research combined field and laboratory methods to detect positive Darwinian selection (i.e. adaptive evolution) at the molecular level in natural populations.  In addition to technical articles, he has published in the [[London Review of Books]],<ref name="LRB1">{{cite magazine|title=London Review of Books|url=http://www.lrb.co.uk/v22/n10/andrew-berry/an-ugly-baby|magazine=An Ugly Baby: Alfred Russel Wallace|date=18 May 2000 |volume=22 |issue=10 |publisher=London Review of Books|last1=Berry |first1=Andrew }}</ref><ref name="LRB2">{{cite magazine|title=London Review of Books|url=http://www.lrb.co.uk/v22/n03/andrew-berry/data-guy|magazine=Data Guy: Charles Darwin|date=3 February 2000 |volume=22 |issue=3 |publisher=London Review of Books|last1=Berry |first1=Andrew }}</ref><ref name="LRB3">{{cite magazine|title=London Review of Books|url=http://www.lrb.co.uk/v25/n03/andrew-berry/reasons-for-being-nice-and-having-sex|magazine=W D Hamilton|date=6 February 2003 |volume=25 |issue=3 |publisher=London Review of Books|last1=Berry |first1=Andrew }}</ref> [[Slate (magazine)|Slate]],<ref name="Slate1">{{cite web|title=Slate|url=http://www.slate.com/articles/briefing/articles/1997/03/sheep_thrills.html|work=Dolly the Cloned Sheep|date=2 March 1997 |publisher=Slate}}</ref> and elsewhere.  He has published two books: ''Infinite tropics: an Alfred Russel Wallace anthology'', 2003, with a foreword written by [[Stephen Jay Gould]],<ref name="Berry1">{{cite book|author1=Alfred Russel Wallace |author2=Andrew Berry |author3=Stephen Jay Gould |title=Infinite tropics: an Alfred Russel Wallace anthology|year=2003|publisher=Verso|isbn=9781859844786 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ieH8TltPmzIC}}</ref> and ''DNA: The Secret of Life'' with [[James Watson]], 2003.<ref name="Berry2">{{cite book|last=Berry|first=Andrew|title=DNA: The Secret of Life|year=2008|publisher=Paw Prints|isbn=9781435290709|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-953PwAACAAJ}}</ref> In addition to lecturing at Harvard, he also leads a Harvard Summer Study Abroad program at [[Queen's College, Oxford]] on the history of evolutionary biology and on current ideas in the field.<ref name="Summer1">{{cite web|title=Oxford, England |url=http://www.summer.harvard.edu/2012/programs/abroad/oxford/ |work=Harvard Summer School }}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>  He teaches evolutionary biology regularly at [[Sabancı University]] in Istanbul, Turkey, and is accordingly targeted by Turkish creationist organizations.<ref name="HY1">{{cite web|title=Harun Yahya|url=http://harunyahya.com/en/works/14429/darwinists-now-raise-their-hopes|work=Pagan American Priest Importing Darwinism to Turkey|publisher=Harun Yahya}}</ref>

Berry has worked on the script development for several major TV shows: ''Race, the Power of an Illusion'' in 2003 by [[Public Broadcasting Service|PBS]],<ref>{{cite web|title=PBS credits|url=https://www.pbs.org/race/000_About/002_04-credits-03.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030424015120/http://www.pbs.org/race/000_About/002_04-credits-03.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 April 2003|work=Credits|publisher=PBS}}</ref> the 5-part [[Channel 4]] ''DNA'',<ref name="Web1">{{cite web|title=Harvard |url=http://www.hmnh.harvard.edu/travel/nav_leader_bios.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030804235349/http://www.hmnh.harvard.edu/travel/nav_leader_bios.html |url-status = dead|archive-date=2003-08-04 |publisher=Harvard University }}</ref> and [[Nova (American TV series)|NOVA]]'s ''Lord of the Ants''.<ref>{{cite web|title=TV program credits|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/eowilson/credits.html|publisher=PBS}}</ref> In 2013, along with George Beccaloni, curator with a special interest in Orthopteroidea and the Alfred Russel Wallace collections at the [[Natural History Museum, London]], Berry narrated a short animated film for ''The New York Times'' to celebrate the Alfred Russel Wallace's centenary.<ref name="Litchman">{{cite web|last=Litchman|first=Flora|title=The Animated Life of A.R. Wallace|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/11/05/opinion/the-animated-life-of-ar-wallace.html|work=The New York Times|accessdate=7 November 2013|author2=Sharon Shattuck|date=4 November 2013}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married to Harvard Professor [[Naomi Pierce]], and they have twin children.

Berry was pranked during a comedy video where [[YouTuber]], [[JiDion]] crashed a Life Sciences lecture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2022/3/2/youtubers-disguised-crash-classes/|website=[[The Harvard Crimson]]|title=YouTubers Disguised as Harvard Students Crash Classes|access-date=2022-09-28}}</ref>
